title: Licensing & State Laws
summary: What your license and permit allow, how teen licensing, insurance and points work, the records you must keep current, how to handle a traffic stop, and your duties after a crash.

blocks.text: Driving is a privilege, not a right. You earn it by meeting your state's licensing rules, and the state can take it away if you break serious traffic laws.

rows: Suspended
Your privilege to drive is taken away for a time. You may not drive until it is restored, and driving while suspended brings more penalties.
Revoked
Your privilege is cancelled. You must meet your state's rules to get a license again.
State ID card
Proves who you are only. It does not let you drive.

items: Carry your license any time you drive, and show it to an officer who asks. Officers also ask for your registration and proof of insurance, so keep them in the car.
Hold the right license class for the vehicle. A regular car license does not cover a motorcycle; you need a motorcycle license or endorsement.

blocks.text: Passing the knowledge test (along with your state's vision test and other requirements) gets you a learner permit, not the right to drive alone. A permit holder may drive only with a qualified licensed driver in the car.
A parent's permission does not replace the supervisor's presence, even for a two-block trip. Supervisor age and seating rules vary; see your State Cheat Sheet.
Most states use graduated licensing for young drivers. It usually works in three stages:

items: Learner permit: drive only with a qualified supervisor.
Intermediate (provisional) license: drive alone, but with limits, often on late-night driving and on how many young passengers you carry.
Full license: the limits end once you meet your state's age and time requirements.

blocks.text: Permit ages, practice hours, night hours and passenger limits vary a lot by state. Check your State Cheat Sheet.

items: Never lend your license or use someone else's. Both are illegal and can cost you your driving privilege.
Never change any information on a license, such as the birth date, or show a license you know is altered or fake.
Do not let an unlicensed person drive your car, even around the block. Riding along does not make it legal unless they hold a permit and you meet the supervisor rules.
If you knowingly let someone with a suspended license drive your car, you can be penalized too, not just the driver.

rows: Insurance
Every state has financial responsibility laws, and most require vehicle owners to carry liability insurance. Minimum coverage varies by state.
Points
Many states add points to your driving record for moving violations. Too many points in a set time can lead to a warning, a required course, or suspension.
Losing your license
Common causes include impaired driving, refusing a chemical test, leaving a crash scene, too many points and driving without insurance.

blocks.text: Point values, limits and insurance minimums are state-specific. See your State Cheat Sheet.

rows: You move within the state
Report your new address to the driver licensing agency by your state's deadline. Telling the post office does not update your driver record.
You move to a new state
Get the new state's license within the time its law allows, usually by turning in your old one. Visitors may drive on a valid home-state license; new residents cannot do so forever.
Vehicle registration
The owner must know when it expires and renew on time. No reminder in the mail is not an excuse.
License plates
Keep them clean, visible and readable. Tinted or dark covers that hide the characters are not allowed.

blocks.text: Deadlines for address changes and for new residents vary by state. Check your State Cheat Sheet.

sections.heading: When police signal you to stop

items: Turn on your signal to show you have seen the officer.
Move to the right side of the road and stop as soon as it is safe, even if you are in the far left lane, unless the officer tells you otherwise. Do not stop on a curve or in the median.
Do not stop suddenly in a traffic lane.
Once stopped, put the car in Park, turn off the engine and radio, and wait for the officer.

blocks.text: If an unmarked car signals you on a dark, empty road and you are unsure it is a real officer, turn on your flashers, slow down, and drive to a nearby well-lit, busy place. You can call 911 to confirm. Never flee or ignore the lights.

blocks.caption: When you pass a police car or other emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, move over a lane if you safely can, or slow down. Move-over rules vary; see your State Cheat Sheet.

items: You and your passengers stay inside the car unless the officer tells you to get out.
Keep your hands in plain view, such as on top of the steering wheel, and avoid sudden movements.
At night, turn on the interior (dome) light so the officer can see inside.
If your documents are out of reach, such as in a bag in the back seat, tell the officer where they are and wait for permission before reaching.
If asked to step out, do so carefully, watch for traffic, keep your hands visible and stand where the officer directs.

blocks.text: If you think a ticket is unfair, stay calm and respectful. Do not argue at the roadside; you can contest it later in court.

Every driver involved in a crash must stop, help anyone who is hurt, and exchange the required information, no matter who caused it or how small the damage. Crash-reporting rules vary; see your State Cheat Sheet.
Leaving the scene without stopping is a hit-and-run, with severe penalties, especially if someone is hurt. If you panic and drive off, go back to the scene right away.

keyPoints: Driving is a privilege that can be suspended or revoked; a state ID card does not let you drive.
Carry your license whenever you drive, and hold the right class for the vehicle.
A permit holder must always have a qualified licensed supervisor in the car; teen license limits vary by state.
Never lend, alter or borrow a license, and never let an unlicensed or suspended driver use your car.
Keep required insurance; too many points on your record can cost you your license.
Report address changes and get a new-state license by your state's deadlines; renew registration on time and keep plates readable.
When police signal, signal and pull right; stay in the car with hands visible and the dome light on at night.
Always stop after a crash you are involved in; leaving is a hit-and-run.
